hits.text: 3 School mental health screening is defined as the use of a systematic tool or process to identify the strengths and needs of students. Screening is conducted for all students, not just students identified as being at risk for or already displaying mental health concerns. This might involve screening an entire population, such as a school’s student body, or a smaller subset of a population, such as a specific grade level. Most commonly, mental health screening is used to identify individual students who are experiencing or are at risk of experiencing social, emotional, and/or behavioral difficulties. The use of screening as an early identification strategy detects the onset of challenges early so that they can be addressed before they escalate. Screening measures can also ask students about: • indicators of well-being and positive mental health • life satisfaction • school belonging • social determinants of mental health • adverse early life experiences What is School Mental Health Screening? hits.text: DEPRESSION SCREENING IN COLLEGE STUDENTS 6 injury, and possibly suicide (Pedrelli el al., 2015). Mental illnesses such as depression has been associated with significant morbidity, mortality, disability, and increased risk of suicide (Khubchandani, Brey, Kotecki, Kleinfelder, & Anderson, 2016). Efforts to increase awareness and screening of depression among college students should be a priority. Local Problem An identified public college health center had a complaint-based approach to depression screening. A complaint-based approach screens for depression if a patient presented with depression-related symptoms. Patients may mask their depressive symptoms and suicidal intent by complaining of other health issues. Patients may report somatic symptoms in an attempt to avoid mental health stigma. Thus, the complaint-based approach may under-detect and under- treat depression. The Patient Health Questionnaire-2 (PHQ-2) could be utilized as a first step approach to screen college students for depression during every visit at the college health center. The PHQ-2 has two questions and can easily be administered by healthcare providers at the college health center. College students who screen positive should be further evaluated with the PHQ-9 and possibly referred to counseling services at the identified public college. The counseling center at the identified public college provides an array of mental health services that could be beneficial for college students who are experiencing depression, but college students should first be screened and identified. Clinical Question In college-aged students (P), how does screening for depression with the Patient Health Questionnaire-2 (PHQ-2) (I) compared to current practice (C) affect early identification of depression (O)?

Inform Prevention and Early Intervention Strategies • About 20% of students show signs and symptoms of a mental health disorder in a given year. Mental health screening is a proactive approach to gathering valuable information for planning and implementing prevention and early intervention strategies for the other 80% before problems develop or worsen. • When schools systematically ask students about indicators of well-being and social-emotional distress, they gather information that enables them to implement targeted prevention and early intervention strategies that can address the unique needs of a school or community. • Example: If screening reveals high levels of student stress and anxiety, teaching coping skills to help reduce anxiety may be a helpful strategy to implement in classrooms. Screening with follow-up support can also detect and address student mental health problems early before they escalate. Why Screen?
